Go TUI on Bubble Tea v2 over the `tasks` tracker. It shells out to the `tasks` binary
and reads its JSON; it never opens `tasks/*.md`.

## Setup

Work in a worktree under .worktrees/ (`git worktree add`), then `just setup`: it
downloads the Go modules and points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks`.

## Gates

    just gate

`just check` (seconds): `tools/ops-check`, `tools/ops-docs check`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `tasks check`.
`just test`: `go test ./...` — the integration test skips when `tasks` is not on `PATH`.
`just docs` regenerates the identity and family regions of README.md and AGENTS.md
from identity.toml and tools/family.toml; edit those files, never the regions.
Rebuild from the main checkout after changes merge: `just install` replaces the
`tasks-tui` and `tui` on `PATH`, so never run it in a worktree.
Fixtures under internal/tasksctl/testdata/ are recaptured with `just capture <name> <tasks
args>`, which pipes live output through `tools/scrub-fixtures`; raw `tasks` output is never
committed.

## Layout

- `cmd/tasks-tui/` — flags, config, startup probe, program.
- internal/tasksctl/ — the only subprocess boundary: `Runner`, typed calls, JSON types, `Error`, `CheckoutFor`.
- internal/identity/ — familiar's slot algorithm (remote key, pins, fnv1a32, hue table, tone).
- internal/launch/ — harness commands and the terminal spawn.
- internal/config/ — `~/.config/tasks-tui/config.toml`.
- internal/ui/ — the Bubble Tea model: app, views, the shared task form, overlays, styles, the column model (columns.go), the legend.

## Rules

- This repo adopts the tasks skill's process and workspace policy: the task's `process`
  field, not a generic Superpowers trigger, decides whether brainstorming runs.
- The JSON contract belongs to `tasks`; anything the TUI needs and cannot get is a task there, never a workaround here.
- A missing required field is a decode error. Sparse task optional fields and empty collections may be omitted. Fail early with a typed error; no silent fallbacks.
- No `--agent` on `add`: a person files from the TUI, and an agent stamp would misattribute it.
